| Codex CLI (GPT-5.6 Sol) | 256 | 199 | 189 | 3 | 186 | 0.738 | 0.727 |
| Fable 5.1 (Terminus 2) | 256 | 216 | 216 | 3 | 213 | 0.844 | 0.832 |
| GPT-6 Astra (Terminus 2) | 256 | 212 | 212 | 3 | 209 | 0.828 | 0.816 |
| All | 1024 | 840 | 801 | 12 | 789 | 0.782 | 0.770 |

All numbers Lean-checked. Of the 840 accepted runs, 12 fail condition 5 whether or not they were dropped for the axiom rule (the 12 are all outside the 39 axiom drops); without the axiom rule the count would be 828. The solver order is unchanged (Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra, Codex CLI, Claude Code). Counted passes by prover class (a reading): trivial 658, identical or near-identical 74, neither 57.

**How it was checked.** `lean/GoldChkLib.lean` adds the command `#gold_check`. Compiled at the end of each run's unchanged bridge file (Lean 4.22.0, Mathlib, skampere1; `scripts/runone_gold_names.sh`), it lists every user-written theorem in the namespace `Gold` of the imported gold module (declaration ranges present, so no compiler-generated names) and looks up its counterpart: `Bridge.G_<name>`, or `Bridge.G_<parent>_<name>` when the last component is ambiguous or namespaced (bridges use this for gold files with several layers, e.g. `G_RealLayer_half_product_thm`). It requires the counterpart to be a theorem whose transitive axioms are only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`. Not required (logged separately): private helper lemmas (488 in 103 runs), structure-field proofs (2, one task: `nonempty`) and lemmas nested in another declaration (18 in 6 runs, e.g. `non_empty_thm.aux_mono`). 4,647 gold names over the 840 runs; 4,635 proved. All 840 checks compiled with exit 0 and no error. `scripts/gold_name_check.py` writes `results/gold_name_check.json` (per run: names, missing, exclusions, reason), `results/gold_name_check_summary.json`, and appends `all_gold_names_proved` (1/0, blank where Lean did not accept the proof) and `counted_all5` to `results/per_run.csv`; existing columns are unchanged. Per-run logs (filtered to the check lines): `lean/gold_name_logs_tiny.tgz`.

**Controls (Lean-checked, `results/gold_name_controls.json`, files in `lean/gold_name_controls/`).** Scratch copies of the W2_104 bridge (5 gold names), originals untouched: the unchanged copy passes 5 of 5; renaming one counterpart to `G_overflow_denies_thm_renamed` is flagged `MISSING`; deleting that theorem is flagged `MISSING`; replacing its proof by `sorry` is flagged `NONSTD [sorryAx]`.

**Choices that move the number.**
- Public helper lemmas count as named theorems (strict reading of "each named theorem"). Excluding the 12 helper-lemma runs would give 801, the old count. They are the only reason any of the 840 fail; if you decide helper lemmas are not named theorems, say so and the rule text changes with the counts.
- A first checker version flagged 22 runs; 10 of those were checker artifacts (namespaced `G_` names, structure fields, nested auxiliary lemmas) and are fixed in `GoldChkLib.lean`; the first-version logs are not kept.
- The check shows a bridge theorem exists and is proved. That its statement is the gold statement transported through the adapter is a reading, not Lean-checked (see Caveats).
- The harsh int_ref numbers above were not recomputed after condition 5; in the per-run DT file none of the 12 runs is a harsh int_ref DT pass.

## Conclusion for today (11-04-2026): prover-based FSC (proposed for co-author review, not yet a rule)
**Proposed statement.** We provisionally retain prover-based FSC as supplementary evidence of directional coverage (Agent.FS implies GoldRef.FS) verified under a fixed proof-search budget. A failure means "not proved under this setup", not a demonstrated specification gap. Integrity gaps were found in the raw pipeline; real-output accuracy and ranking reliability are not validated. The missing human ratings come first. (Statement from the independent validation in veribench-inf experiment 12, commit 4f97c875; the numbers below are from this experiment's data, receipts in `results/ruler_validity_phase0.json`, script `scripts/ruler_validity_phase0.py`, no model calls.)

**What this experiment adds** (counts are over the 789 counted runs under conditions 1 to 5 unless stated; Lean-checked unless marked reading).
- **Task difficulty dominates.** Of the variance in counted pass over 256 tasks x 4 solver agents, 70% is the task, 1.7% the solver, 28% task x solver (ICC(1) of task 0.605). 154 tasks pass for all four solvers, 35 for none; only 67 tasks (1 to 3 solvers pass) can separate solvers. 196 of the 256 tasks are security tasks (pass rate 0.74 to 0.88 per solver; HumanEval 0.45 to 0.59, real code 0.08 to 0.58, CS 0.40 to 0.50).
- **Two tiers, not four ranks.** Paired bootstrap over tasks (5,000 resamples): Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra beat Codex CLI and Claude Code by 0.09 to 0.125 (every 95% interval excludes 0); Fable 5.1 vs Astra [-0.016, 0.047] and Codex CLI vs Claude Code [-0.074, 0.035] are not separated. P(Fable > Astra > Codex > Claude Code) = 0.65. No prover repeat variance was measured, and the tier gap cannot be told apart from how bridgeable each solver's representation is.
- **Most credited passes are low-information.** The prover's own class (reading): 732 of 789 are trivial or identical (658 + 74). Brando's note stands: an A to A pass is not cheating; the consequence is that a 0.8 is mostly easy tasks.
- **Ungrounded passes (script over `gold_without_agent_hyp`, a reading).** 51 of 789 counted runs have at least one gold theorem proved without any agent hypothesis (2 have all); 66 of 4,206 gold theorems (30 runs have no value). Those pass for any agent, including an empty spec. Candidate condition 6 (flag, not applied).
- **Failures are mostly unresolved, not demonstrated.** Of the 184 runs Lean did not accept, 60 have a bridge JSON: 52 not proved with no counter-model claimed, 5 with a prover-claimed counter-model (reading, not Lean-checked), 3 where the solver's own file did not compile; 124 have no bridge JSON and are unclassified.
- **The pass set depends on the prover pipeline.** The saved gpipe bridges of veribench-inf experiment 12 (a different bridge set under the same module ids, Gemini low) clear a mechanical gate (every public gold name, allowed axioms, no NOT_PROVED marker) on 687 of 1,024 runs, versus 789 here. On per-run pass/fail the two agree on 842 of 1,024 (0.82, Cohen kappa 0.56): both 647, only here 142, only there 40, neither 195. The gates differ and neither adjudicates faithfulness, so this is evidence that the score reflects the prover and bridge, not a measured error rate.

**Pros.** An accepted, faithful proof is mathematical evidence of the implication, stronger than a model's reading. Only one direction is needed. A 0.80 can mean at least 0.80 verified coverage once every credited success is integrity-checked.
**Cons.** Lean checks the supplied proposition, not whether the bridge and adapter state the right one (174 of the 759 counted runs with a known adapter use a semantic encoding, a reading). Conditions 1 to 5 do not block a bridge that reuses the gold's own proof (veribench-inf experiment 12: the raw rule accepts 6 of 7 invalid controls, the name and axiom gates alone 3 of 7). Scores reflect proof difficulty, representation and prover budget as well as coverage, so a harsher ruler is not automatically a better one.
**Not established.** Whether prover-based FSC beats the FSC judge on accuracy or ranking (needs the same human-rated items); faithfulness of the 789 bridges; prover repeat variance; agreement with smooth FSC rankings.

## Per-run tables
`results/table_<solver>.csv`, one per solver agent, 256 rows: task, run id, U (ub9sc), Lean entails, axioms ok, non-vacuous, counted, drop reason, offending theorems. Axioms and non-vacuous are `n/a` where the entailment proof was not accepted (nothing to check). `results/per_run.csv` has all 1,024 with the raw experiment 142 flag kept as `lean_entails_raw`; `results/dropped_runs.md` lists the 39.

## What was checked, how
- Entailment: experiment 142 (Lean proofs, unchanged).
- Axioms: `#print axioms` for every named `Agent.*` theorem of the 840 runs (`results/ax_result.json`, logs in `lean/axiom_logs_tiny.tgz`). 39 runs have at least one theorem on `Lean.ofReduceBool`. (A first pass skipped theorems whose namespace contains `match_` or `proof_` as text; `AxLib` now skips only auxiliary names, and the 56 affected runs were rerun: same 39 flagged.)
- Gold unedited: `results/gold_check_waves.json` (840 of 840 same).
- Witnesses: 840 witness files (`lean/witnesses_tiny.tgz`), 796 generated and compiled as is, 44 with a hand-written override for a hypothesis `decide` could not close (String functions defined by well-founded recursion, e.g. `toInt?`, `splitOn`, `substrEq.loop`; the files are in the same archive under `witnesses_hand_written_overrides`). All 840 compiled with `WITNESS_OK` and the standard axioms (`results/nonvacuity_witness_status.json`, logs in `lean/witness_logs_tiny.tgz`).
- Static scan of the 840 agent, gold and bridge files for `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, `unsafe`, `implemented_by`, `extern`, `opaque`, `native_decide`, macros and attributes (`results/static_check.json`): no `sorry`, no added axiom, no `implemented_by` / `extern` / `opaque`. The `unsafe` hit is an identifier (`unsafe_thm`), and the few macro and attribute hits (agent 1 and 3, bridge 3, gold 3) were read and are benign. `native_decide` appears as text in all 840 agent files and 812 gold files because the VeriBench format has unit-test `example ... := by native_decide` lines; an `example` is not a named theorem, nothing uses it, and it is outside the axiom rule's scope (every named theorem and the entailment proof). The 39 dropped runs are the ones where a named agent theorem itself depends on `native_decide`.

## Caveats
- A witness shows the agent's spec is satisfiable on the real agent definitions. It does not show the bridge states the agent's theorems exactly as the agent wrote them; that is a reading. It also does not detect an unsatisfiable `Pre` inside an agent theorem the gold does not use; entailment through the gold's own preconditions covers the gold-relevant ones.
- The `native_decide` rule is applied literally. The 39 dropped runs have accepted entailment proofs and witnesses; without the rule the count is 840.
- Lean-checked counts are lower bounds (a failed proof can be a prover miss).

## Files
`scripts/aggregate2.py` (counted flag; run `python3 aggregate2.py <data> <experiments> <out> tiny_status.json`, `tiny_status.json` is in `results/`), `scripts/dt_metrics.py` (experiment 143's script with `--per_run`), `agg_w.py`, `mk_one.py` (witness generator), `static_check.py`, `axrun.sh`, `run1c.sh`; `lean/WitLib.lean`, `lean/AxLib.lean`.

=== 142 README ===
# Experiment 142: Lean-checked "agent spec implies gold spec" for all 1,024 Tiny-256 runs (no DT)

> **Update (Nov 1, 2026, experiment 145).** The 840 below are the runs where Lean accepted the entailment proof. Two more checks now apply: the agent's spec must be non-vacuous (a concrete witness) and no agent theorem may depend on `native_decide` or any non-standard axiom. 0 of the 840 are vacuous; 39 depend on `native_decide` (Claude Code 29, Codex CLI 10). The counted passes are **801 of 1,024**: Claude Code 184, Codex CLI 189, Fable 5.1 216, GPT-6 Astra 212. Harsh int_ref (no DT) is unchanged. Use the experiment 145 numbers; read the 840 below as "entailment accepted, before the two checks".

No DT (no differential testing). Tiny-256 only (public tasks); the private set is not in this folder.

## What this is
For each run (one task x one solver agent, 4 x 256 = 1,024) a Lean proof was written by ub9sc (the prover; helper agents of ub9sc) that every public gold theorem follows from the theorems the solver agent's own Lean file states. Lean accepts or rejects it. This replaces the two readings of experiment 140 (U = ub9sc reading, G = Gemini reading), which were opinions of a checker, not proofs.

Labels. **Lean-checked** = the bridge file compiles, every public gold theorem is proved, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, no sorry / admit / native_decide. **Reading** = a yes/no or class label a prover assigned by reading the two files (U, G, the class and adapter-kind columns). A failed Lean proof can be a false fail (the prover did not find the proof) but never a false pass, so the Lean-checked rate is a lower bound.

## Result (Lean-checked, no DT)
Bottom line: Lean accepts agent implies gold on **840 of 1,024 runs (0.820)**, a lower bound. By solver agent: Claude Code (Opus 5) 213/256, Codex CLI (GPT-5.6 Sol) 199/256, Fable 5.1 (Terminus 2) 216/256, GPT-6 Astra (Terminus 2) 212/256. ub9sc's readings were right on 986 of the 1,020 runs it judged (834 of its 866 passes are Lean-checked; 2 of its 154 fails are); Gemini's on 948 of 1,024 (797 of 830 passes; 43 of 194 fails are Lean-checked). The entailment passes are shallow: of 809 Lean-checked passes in the 980 wave runs, 676 are classed trivial (gold theorems follow in one or two routine steps from an agent theorem), 76 identical or near-identical, 57 neither (readings). With entailment (Lean-checked) in place of the judged theorem coverage, harsh int_ref (no DT) is 0 at the floor and at most 10 of 1,024 at the high end (1 to 6 per solver agent; see below), so Tiny-256 stays not saturated.

| Solver agent | Runs | Lean-checked entails | Rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Claude Code (Opus 5) | 256 | 213 | 0.832 |
| Codex CLI (GPT-5.6 Sol) | 256 | 199 | 0.777 |
| Fable 5.1 (Terminus 2) | 256 | 216 | 0.844 |
| GPT-6 Astra (Terminus 2) | 256 | 212 | 0.828 |
| All | 1024 | 840 | 0.820 |

Lean-checked count by what each checker said (denominator = runs with that reading):

| Solver agent | U=1 | U=0 | G=1 | G=0 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Claude Code (Opus 5) | 210/218 | 2/37 | 202/209 | 11/47 |
| Codex CLI (GPT-5.6 Sol) | 198/210 | 0/45 | 189/199 | 10/57 |
| Fable 5.1 (Terminus 2) | 215/221 | 0/34 | 205/212 | 11/44 |
| GPT-6 Astra (Terminus 2) | 211/217 | 0/38 | 201/210 | 11/46 |
| All | 834/866 | 2/154 | 797/830 | 43/194 |

4 runs have no U reading (ub9sc did not judge them): 1,020 judged.

harsh int and harsh int_ref (no DT), entailment = Lean-checked (floor to high end: an unrun check counts failed at the floor and passed at the high end, as in experiments 137 and 138; the floor is 0 for all four):

| Solver agent | harsh int, high end | harsh int_ref, high end |
|---|---:|---:|
| Claude Code (Opus 5) | 2 | 2 |
| Codex CLI (GPT-5.6 Sol) | 2 | 1 |
| Fable 5.1 (Terminus 2) | 44 | 6 |
| GPT-6 Astra (Terminus 2) | 9 | 1 |

Per-task tables, one per solver agent (columns task, U, G, Lean; 0/1): `results/per_task_<solver>.csv`. Per-run data with every check: `results/per_run.csv`; totals: `results/summary.json`, `results/tables.md`.

## Checks per run (acceptance list)
- Compiles, axioms, no sorry: `lean/blogs/<mod>.log` (per-theorem `#print axioms`). All 840 Lean-checked passes use only the three allowed axioms and no sorry / admit / native_decide (809 of 809 wave passes by script; 31 of 31 sample passes in experiment 141).
- Agent precondition satisfiable: every agent file of a Lean-checked pass is sorry-free (the agent's own functions are a model of its theorems), so the hypotheses are not contradictory. This also rules out an agent postcondition that is false for every input.
- Gold postcondition not trivially true: gold theorems proved without using any agent hypothesis: in 53 of the 809 wave passes at least one gold theorem, in 2 all of them. Column `gold_without_agent_hyp` in per_run.csv (counted by script on the proof text, a heuristic).
- Adapter noted per run: `adapter_kind` (cast-only 617, semantic encoding 192 among the 809 wave passes; sorted by a keyword rule on the prover's adapter text, so a reading) and the adapter text in `results/wave_K.jsonl`. A semantic encoding means "entailed modulo the adapter"; faithfulness of the adapter is a reading, not Lean-checked.
- Proof length: `proof_lines` = non-blank, non-comment lines of all gold theorem proofs in the bridge; median 31 per run (809 wave passes), longest 127.

## Not Lean-checked (184 runs)
179 compile but not every gold theorem is proved (Float / Real versus Rat, ASCII versus Unicode digits, differing models, gold parts with no natural adapter), 5 do not compile (T39, the heap_sort bridge of the sample, 3 theorems with errors; W6_000, where the solver agent's own file does not compile; W7_111; W8_017 and W8_074, which have no bridge). A prover that did not find a proof may still be a false fail, so these 184 are not shown to be non-entailed.

## Method
1. `scripts/prep_wave.py` wraps gold and agent files (`namespace Gold` / `namespace Agent`) from `results/waves/wave_K.json`; they compile as separate modules (Lean v4.22.0 with Mathlib, skampere1, `scripts/build.sh`, `queue_runner.sh`).
2. ub9sc helper agents write `Bridge_<mod>.lean`: the agent's theorem statements become hypotheses about abstract function variables, so its definitions cannot be unfolded; each public gold theorem is transported to the agent functions through an explicit adapter and proved from them. One prover per two runs, compile (`bridge.sh`, `runbridges.sh`), at most two fix rounds on compile errors, then the theorem is left in a `-- NOT_PROVED:` comment and the run does not count.
3. `scripts/review_wave.py` computes the checks per run; `scripts/aggregate.py` joins them with U and G (experiment 140), experiment 137 and 138 per-task components and writes the tables. Run: `python3 scripts/aggregate.py <data_dir with review.json and scale/{waves,results}> <experiments dir> <out dir>`.
4. 1,024 runs = the 44-run sample of experiment 141 (`results/review_sample44.json`) + 8 waves (7 x 123 + 119 runs; `results/wave_K.jsonl`).

## Files
- `lean/bridges/Bridge_<mod>.lean|json`: final bridge per run (978 of 980 wave runs have one, plus 44 sample); `lean/blogs/`: compile logs. Gold and agent sources are regenerated by `prep_wave.py` from the manifests. Run to module map: `per_run.csv` columns `run`, `mod`.
- `results/`, `scripts/`: above.

## Caveats
Provers are ub9sc only; Gemini as a Lean prover is a separate follow-up. U and G are readings. The class (trivial, identical, neither) and adapter kind are readings. 752 of the 809 wave passes (93 percent) are classed trivial or identical by reading; a Lean-checked pass is weak evidence that the agent spec is strong. The 44-run sample is stratified toward disagreements, but it is part of the 1,024 so every run has a Lean result.

=== 140 PROTOCOL ===
# Entailment check protocol (theorem coverage by entailment)

For one cell you get two Lean 4 files for the same task: GOLD (the reference: implementation, tests, public theorem statements) and AGENT (a solver agent's own Lean file: implementation and its own theorem statements, possibly with proofs or `sorry`).

Question: does the AGENT's specification entail the GOLD's specification? Same or stronger passes; equivalence is not required. No pairing of every agent theorem with every gold theorem is wanted: reason with one master spec on each side.

Definitions
- Master spec of GOLD, M_G: the conjunction of the statements of GOLD's public theorems (theorem/lemma with a statement about the task's functions; skip `example`, `#eval`, private helper lemmas that are only proof steps, and statements that are only unit tests of concrete values). Statements are read as precondition => postcondition about the gold function(s) f_G.
- Master spec of AGENT, M_A: the conjunction of the statements of AGENT's theorems about its function(s) f_A (the same reading). Proof status is NOT part of the check (a `sorry` proof still states the spec); a statement that does not typecheck or that is vacuous (hypotheses contradictory, conclusion trivially true) contributes nothing.
- Interface adapter: the map from gold's function(s) and types to the agent's (names may differ, Nat vs Int, List vs Array, Option vs Except, extra fuel or error cases are fine when the adapter is stated explicitly and natural). If no natural adapter exists, entails = 0.
- ENTAILS = 1 iff, for an arbitrary f_A that satisfies M_A (nothing else assumed about f_A, not its definition), each gold theorem in M_G, translated through the adapter, follows logically from M_A (plus standard facts about the data types). Stated preconditions: gold's precondition must imply agent's precondition (the agent may not demand more of the inputs than gold does).
- Do NOT use the agent's implementation or its proofs to argue entailment; only its stated spec. Do NOT penalise a stronger or extra agent theorem.
- A gold theorem that merely restates a concrete implementation detail of f_G that the task description does not require (for example exact tie-breaking, a specific error string) still counts: if M_A does not imply it, it is not entailed.

Procedure per cell
1. Read GOLD and AGENT. List gold public theorems (G1..Gk) with one-line plain-language meaning, and the agent's theorems (A1..Am) likewise.
2. State the adapter in one line.
3. For each Gi: entailed (which Aj give it, one line) or not entailed (what is missing, one line).
4. entails = 1 iff all Gi entailed (k >= 1). If GOLD has no public theorem statement (k = 0), set entails = null and say so. If AGENT has no theorem statement, entails = 0 (reason no_agent_theorems).
5. Write ONE JSON line to the output file given in your brief, with keys:
   cell (string, as given), entails (1, 0 or null), k_gold (int), k_entailed (int), n_agent_theorems (int), adapter (short string), not_entailed (list of "Gname: reason", at most 5, each under 25 words), confidence ("high"|"medium"|"low"), why (under 40 words, plain words), uncertain_reason (only if confidence is not high).
Use plain standard terms (precondition, postcondition, theorem, entails). Do not look at any score for the cell (you are not given one) and do not search the repository for scores or earlier judgments.

Clarifications (apply to every cell)
- Gold theorems about the gold implementation's own runtime details (Python-specific float, overflow, termination, exact error values) are part of M_G and count; if M_A does not imply them they are not entailed.
- A fuel-bounded or bounded-input agent entails gold's unbounded termination or completeness theorem only if its stated theorems cover that input range.
- A gold theorem relating two gold functions (functional vs imperative, spec vs implementation) is mapped to the agent's counterparts; the agent needs both counterparts and a theorem that relates them or implies the claim.
- A gold conjunction theorem counts once as one theorem; a private or helper lemma that is only a proof step is not public.
- An agent that formalizes the opposite design (for example a vulnerable version where gold models the safe one) has no natural adapter: entails = 0.
- Preconditions are checked per gold theorem: the gold theorem's own hypotheses alone must be enough for the agent's stated theorems to give the conclusion (an extra bound or sortedness hypothesis that the agent requires and the gold theorem lacks is a gap).
- A gold lemma stated for any type with a typeclass (for example any `LT`) is judged at the task's concrete type(s) (for example the one the agent uses with `LinearOrder`); needing a stronger standard instance is not a gap.
- k_gold counts public gold theorem declarations after dropping pure vocabulary or proof-step lemmas; say in `why` if the count is large and you grouped them.

=== 140 LEAN_PROTOCOL ===
# Lean check of an entailment verdict (one run)

You get one run: an AGENT Lean file (a solver agent's implementation and its own theorem statements) and the GOLD Lean file (the reference implementation and its public theorems). Two readers (ub9sc and Gemini) disagreed on whether the agent's stated specification entails the gold's. Your job is to settle it in Lean, not by reading: compile files and report what the compiler says.

Meaning of "entails" (same as PROTOCOL.md in this folder; read it first): for an ARBITRARY function f_A that satisfies only the statements of the agent's theorems (its master spec M_A, nothing else about f_A, not its definition, not the agent's proofs), every public gold theorem (the master spec M_G), translated through a natural interface adapter (Nat/Int, Option/Except, names, extra fuel), must follow. Each gold theorem is judged with its own hypotheses only (an extra bound the agent needs and the gold theorem lacks is a gap).

## What to build (one Lean file per run, `Entail.lean`)
1. Import the same Mathlib modules the gold and agent files import. Copy the vocabulary you need verbatim (inductive types, structures, spec-level predicates, constants) from the agent and gold files. Do NOT copy the implementation of the function being specified.
2. Make the agent's function(s) abstract: take them as `variable`s / theorem arguments, or as fields of a structure. Write the agent's theorem statements, copied verbatim with the function replaced by the abstract one, as hypotheses. Keep each hypothesis's own preconditions exactly as in the agent file. Skip agent statements that only talk about concrete definitions of its own (they say nothing about an arbitrary f_A) and statements that are vacuous.
3. State the adapter in a comment, and define the gold function(s) through it (a `def`/`abbrev` of the abstract agent function).
4. For each gold public theorem, state it with the gold function replaced by the adapter, and try to prove it from the hypotheses: `theorem G_i (f : ...) (h1 : ...) (h2 : ...) : <gold statement> := by ...`.
5. For a gold theorem you cannot prove, decide whether it is really not entailed: build a COUNTER-MODEL in Lean: a second concrete function f' for which you prove ALL the agent hypotheses and prove the negation of the gold theorem. A counter-model that satisfies all hypotheses and breaks the gold theorem is a Lean proof of "not entailed".
6. Compile on the host with `lake env lean`, see below. A theorem counts only if the compiler reports no error and no `sorry` warning for it. Do not use `sorry` and do not add axioms; do not weaken a gold statement to make it provable; do not strengthen an agent hypothesis beyond what the agent file states.

Which gold theorems: `k_gold` can be large. First do the ones the failing reader named (both readers' stated reasons are in your input); if one of those is refuted by a counter-model the run is decided (not entailed) and you can stop. If you want to claim "entailed" you must prove every public gold theorem (group them if the gold file has many; if the gold file has more than 25 public theorems and the named gaps are all proved, prove the rest too or report `partial` with the numbers).

## Compiling (locally, Lean v4.22.0 with Mathlib; subagents cannot use ssh)
- Compile with Bash: `cd /home/agent/lean_vb && PATH=$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH timeout 280 lake env lean /var/lib/agent/scratch/at2297/lean/<run id>/Entail.lean 2>&1 | head -80; echo exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}`. A trivial file takes about 7 seconds; this machine has 1 CPU shared with other jobs, so long files can take minutes: run long compiles with `run_in_background` and read the output file, and keep proofs cheap (prefer `simp`, `omega`, `decide` on small cases over heavy automation).
- Do not touch /home/agent/lean_vb itself (no lake update, no new packages); write only under /var/lib/agent/scratch/at2297/lean/.

# Experiment 142: Lean-checked "agent spec implies gold spec" for all 1,024 Tiny-256 runs (no DT)

> **Update (Nov 1, 2026, experiment 145).** The 840 below are the runs where Lean accepted the entailment proof. Two more checks now apply: the agent's spec must be non-vacuous (a concrete witness) and no agent theorem may depend on `native_decide` or any non-standard axiom. 0 of the 840 are vacuous; 39 depend on `native_decide` (Claude Code 29, Codex CLI 10). The counted passes are **801 of 1,024**: Claude Code 184, Codex CLI 189, Fable 5.1 216, GPT-6 Astra 212. Harsh int_ref (no DT) is unchanged. Use the experiment 145 numbers; read the 840 below as "entailment accepted, before the two checks".

No DT (no differential testing). Tiny-256 only (public tasks); the private set is not in this folder.

## What this is
For each run (one task x one solver agent, 4 x 256 = 1,024) a Lean proof was written by ub9sc (the prover; helper agents of ub9sc) that every public gold theorem follows from the theorems the solver agent's own Lean file states. Lean accepts or rejects it. This replaces the two readings of experiment 140 (U = ub9sc reading, G = Gemini reading), which were opinions of a checker, not proofs.

Labels. **Lean-checked** = the bridge file compiles, every public gold theorem is proved, only the axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, no sorry / admit / native_decide. **Reading** = a yes/no or class label a prover assigned by reading the two files (U, G, the class and adapter-kind columns). A failed Lean proof can be a false fail (the prover did not find the proof) but never a false pass, so the Lean-checked rate is a lower bound.

Bottom line: Lean accepts agent implies gold on **840 of 1,024 runs (0.820)**, a lower bound. === 140 PROTOCOL ===
# Entailment check protocol (theorem coverage by entailment)

For one cell you get two Lean 4 files for the same task: GOLD (the reference: implementation, tests, public theorem statements) and AGENT (a solver agent's own Lean file: implementation and its own theorem statements, possibly with proofs or `sorry`).

Question: does the AGENT's specification entail the GOLD's specification? Same or stronger passes; equivalence is not required. No pairing of every agent theorem with every gold theorem is wanted: reason with one master spec on each side.

Definitions
- Master spec of GOLD, M_G: the conjunction of the statements of GOLD's public theorems (theorem/lemma with a statement about the task's functions; skip `example`, `#eval`, private helper lemmas that are only proof steps, and statements that are only unit tests of concrete values). Statements are read as precondition => postcondition about the gold function(s) f_G.
- Master spec of AGENT, M_A: the conjunction of the statements of AGENT's theorems about its function(s) f_A (the same reading). Proof status is NOT part of the check (a `sorry` proof still states the spec); a statement that does not typecheck or that is vacuous (hypotheses contradictory, conclusion trivially true) contributes nothing.
- Interface adapter: the map from gold's function(s) and types to the agent's (names may differ, Nat vs Int, List vs Array, Option vs Except, extra fuel or error cases are fine when the adapter is stated explicitly and natural). If no natural adapter exists, entails = 0.
- ENTAILS = 1 iff, for an arbitrary f_A that satisfies M_A (nothing else assumed about f_A, not its definition), each gold theorem in M_G, translated through the adapter, follows logically from M_A (plus standard facts about the data types). Stated preconditions: gold's precondition must imply agent's precondition (the agent may not demand more of the inputs than gold does).
- Do NOT use the agent's implementation or its proofs to argue entailment; only its stated spec. Do NOT penalise a stronger or extra agent theorem.
- A gold theorem that merely restates a concrete implementation detail of f_G that the task description does not require (for example exact tie-breaking, a specific error string) still counts: if M_A does not imply it, it is not entailed.

Procedure per cell
1. Read GOLD and AGENT. List gold public theorems (G1..Gk) with one-line plain-language meaning, and the agent's theorems (A1..Am) likewise.
2. State the adapter in one line.
3. For each Gi: entailed (which Aj give it, one line) or not entailed (what is missing, one line).
4. entails = 1 iff all Gi entailed (k >= 1). If GOLD has no public theorem statement (k = 0), set entails = null and say so. If AGENT has no theorem statement, entails = 0 (reason no_agent_theorems).
5. Write ONE JSON line to the output file given in your brief, with keys:
   cell (string, as given), entails (1, 0 or null), k_gold (int), k_entailed (int), n_agent_theorems (int), adapter (short string), not_entailed (list of "Gname: reason", at most 5, each under 25 words), confidence ("high"|"medium"|"low"), why (under 40 words, plain words), uncertain_reason (only if confidence is not high).
Use plain standard terms (precondition, postcondition, theorem, entails). Do not look at any score for the cell (you are not given one) and do not search the repository for scores or earlier judgments.

Clarifications (apply to every cell)
- Gold theorems about the gold implementation's own runtime details (Python-specific float, overflow, termination, exact error values) are part of M_G and count; if M_A does not imply them they are not entailed.
- A fuel-bounded or bounded-input agent entails gold's unbounded termination or completeness theorem only if its stated theorems cover that input range.
- A gold theorem relating two gold functions (functional vs imperative, spec vs implementation) is mapped to the agent's counterparts; the agent needs both counterparts and a theorem that relates them or implies the claim.
- A gold conjunction theorem counts once as one theorem; a private or helper lemma that is only a proof step is not public.
- An agent that formalizes the opposite design (for example a vulnerable version where gold models the safe one) has no natural adapter: entails = 0.
- Preconditions are checked per gold theorem: the gold theorem's own hypotheses alone must be enough for the agent's stated theorems to give the conclusion (an extra bound or sortedness hypothesis that the agent requires and the gold theorem lacks is a gap).
- A gold lemma stated for any type with a typeclass (for example any `LT`) is judged at the task's concrete type(s) (for example the one the agent uses with `LinearOrder`); needing a stronger standard instance is not a gap.
- k_gold counts public gold theorem declarations after dropping pure vocabulary or proof-step lemmas; say in `why` if the count is large and you grouped them.

=== 140 LEAN_PROTOCOL ===
# Lean check of an entailment verdict (one run)

You get one run: an AGENT Lean file (a solver agent's implementation and its own theorem statements) and the GOLD Lean file (the reference implementation and its public theorems). Two readers (ub9sc and Gemini) disagreed on whether the agent's stated specification entails the gold's. Your job is to settle it in Lean, not by reading: compile files and report what the compiler says.

Meaning of "entails" (same as PROTOCOL.md in this folder; read it first): for an ARBITRARY function f_A that satisfies only the statements of the agent's theorems (its master spec M_A, nothing else about f_A, not its definition, not the agent's proofs), every public gold theorem (the master spec M_G), translated through a natural interface adapter (Nat/Int, Option/Except, names, extra fuel), must follow. Each gold theorem is judged with its own hypotheses only (an extra bound the agent needs and the gold theorem lacks is a gap).

## What to build (one Lean file per run, `Entail.lean`)
1. Import the same Mathlib modules the gold and agent files import. Copy the vocabulary you need verbatim (inductive types, structures, spec-level predicates, constants) from the agent and gold files. Do NOT copy the implementation of the function being specified.
2. Make the agent's function(s) abstract: take them as `variable`s / theorem arguments, or as fields of a structure. Write the agent's theorem statements, copied verbatim with the function replaced by the abstract one, as hypotheses. Keep each hypothesis's own preconditions exactly as in the agent file. Skip agent statements that only talk about concrete definitions of its own (they say nothing about an arbitrary f_A) and statements that are vacuous.
3. State the adapter in a comment, and define the gold function(s) through it (a `def`/`abbrev` of the abstract agent function).
4. For each gold public theorem, state it with the gold function replaced by the adapter, and try to prove it from the hypotheses: `theorem G_i (f : ...) (h1 : ...) (h2 : ...) : <gold statement> := by ...`.
5. For a gold theorem you cannot prove, decide whether it is really not entailed: build a COUNTER-MODEL in Lean: a second concrete function f' for which you prove ALL the agent hypotheses and prove the negation of the gold theorem. A counter-model that satisfies all hypotheses and breaks the gold theorem is a Lean proof of "not entailed".
6. Compile on the host with `lake env lean`, see below. A theorem counts only if the compiler reports no error and no `sorry` warning for it. Do not use `sorry` and do not add axioms; do not weaken a gold statement to make it provable; do not strengthen an agent hypothesis beyond what the agent file states.

Which gold theorems: `k_gold` can be large. First do the ones the failing reader named (both readers' stated reasons are in your input); if one of those is refuted by a counter-model the run is decided (not entailed) and you can stop. If you want to claim "entailed" you must prove every public gold theorem (group them if the gold file has many; if the gold file has more than 25 public theorems and the named gaps are all proved, prove the rest too or report `partial` with the numbers).

## Compiling (locally, Lean v4.22.0 with Mathlib; subagents cannot use ssh)
- Compile with Bash: `cd /home/agent/lean_vb && PATH=$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH timeout 280 lake env lean /var/lib/agent/scratch/at2297/lean/<run id>/Entail.lean 2>&1 | head -80; echo exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}`. A trivial file takes about 7 seconds; this machine has 1 CPU shared with other jobs, so long files can take minutes: run long compiles with `run_in_background` and read the output file, and keep proofs cheap (prefer `simp`, `omega`, `decide` on small cases over heavy automation).
- Do not touch /home/agent/lean_vb itself (no lake update, no new packages); write only under /var/lib/agent/scratch/at2297/lean/.
- Budget: about 60 minutes of work per run. If you run out, report what you have.

## Report
Write ONE JSON line to the output file in your brief with keys: cell, lean_verdict ("entails": all gold theorems proved; "not_entails": at least one gold theorem refuted by a compiled counter-model; "undecided": neither), refuted (list of gold theorem names refuted, with a one-line meaning of the counter-model), proved (count) and k_gold, file (local path of Entail.lean), compiled_clean (true only if the final file compiles with exit 0 and no sorry; if you have separate files for counter-models list them), note (under 40 words, plain words: what the missing or the holding fact is). Use "run" or "task", not "cell", in note.
Plain wording. Honest reporting: if a file does not compile, say undecided.

=== GoldChkLib.lean ===
     1	-- TLDR: `#gold_check` lists every user-written named gold theorem (Gold.*) and checks that its bridge counterpart (Bridge.G_<name>, or Bridge.G_<parent>_<name> when the last component is ambiguous or namespaced) exists, is a theorem and uses only standard axioms.
     2	import Lean
     3	open Lean Meta Elab Command
     4	
     5	elab "#gold_check" : command => do
     6	  let env ← getEnv
     7	  -- 1. collect named gold theorems (public, user-written, not structure fields, not nested auxiliaries)
     8	  let mut cands : Array (Name × Name) := #[]
     9	  for (nm, ci) in env.constants.map₁.toList do
    10	    let n' := (privateToUserName? nm).getD nm
    11	    if (`Gold).isPrefixOf n' && (!nm.isInternal || isPrivateName nm) then
    12	      match ci with
    13	      | .thmInfo _ =>
    14	        let aux := match nm.eraseMacroScopes with
    15	          | .str _ l => l.startsWith "match_" || l.startsWith "proof_"
    16	          | _ => false
    17	        if aux then continue
    18	        let rng ← findDeclarationRanges? nm
    19	        if rng.isNone then continue
    20	        if isPrivateName nm then
    21	          logInfo m!"GCHK {n'} PRIVATE_HELPER"
    22	          continue
    23	        let pre := n'.getPrefix
    24	        -- structure field proofs (e.g. `Foo.nonempty` of a structure field) are not named theorems
    25	        match getStructureInfo? env pre with
    26	        | some si =>
    27	          if si.fieldNames.contains (match n' with | .str _ s => Name.mkSimple s | _ => Name.anonymous) then
    28	            logInfo m!"GCHK {n'} STRUCTURE_FIELD"
    29	            continue
    30	        | none => pure ()
    31	        -- nested auxiliary (let rec / local lemma lifted out of another declaration)
    32	        match env.find? pre with
    33	        | some (.thmInfo _) | some (.defnInfo _) =>
    34	          logInfo m!"GCHK {n'} NESTED_AUX"
    35	          continue
    36	        | _ => pure ()
    37	        cands := cands.push (nm, n')
    38	      | _ => pure ()
    39	    else pure ()
    40	  let lastOf := fun (n : Name) => match n with | .str _ s => s | _ => n.toString
    41	  let lasts := cands.map (fun p => lastOf p.2)
    42	  let mut okc := 0
    43	  for (nm, n') in cands do
    44	    let l := lastOf n'
    45	    let dupl := (lasts.filter (· == l)).size > 1
    46	    let parentLast := match n'.getPrefix with | .str _ s => s | _ => ""
    47	    let plain := Name.mkStr `Bridge ("G_" ++ l)
    48	    let qual := Name.mkStr `Bridge ("G_" ++ parentLast ++ "_" ++ l)
    49	    let b? := if dupl then (if (env.find? qual).isSome then some qual else none)
    50	              else if (env.find? plain).isSome then some plain
    51	              else if (env.find? qual).isSome then some qual else none
    52	    match b? with
    53	    | none => logInfo m!"GCHK {n'} MISSING"
    54	    | some b =>
    55	      match env.find? b with
    56	      | some (.thmInfo _) =>
    57	        let ax ← liftCoreM <| collectAxioms b
    58	        let bad := ax.filter (fun a => !(a == ``propext || a == ``Classical.choice || a == ``Quot.sound))
    59	        if bad.size > 0 then logInfo m!"GCHK {n'} NONSTD {bad}"
    60	        else
    61	          okc := okc + 1
    62	          logInfo m!"GCHK {n'} OK {b}"
    63	      | _ => logInfo m!"GCHK {n'} NOT_THEOREM"
    64	  logInfo m!"GSUMMARY gold={cands.size} proved={okc} dup_last_components=0"
=== AxLib.lean ===

     3	open Lean Meta Elab Term Command

     8	  let mut bad := 0

    10	    let n' := (privateToUserName? nm).getD nm
    11	    if (`Agent).isPrefixOf n' && (!nm.isInternal || isPrivateName nm) then

=== WitLib.lean ===
     1	import Mathlib
     2	import Lean
     3	open Lean Meta Elab Term Command
     4	
     5	namespace WitLib
     6	
     7	def agentConsts : MetaM (Array Name × Array Name) := do
     8	  let env ← getEnv
     9	  let mut defs : Array Name := #[]
    10	  let mut thms : Array Name := #[]
    11	  for (n, ci) in env.constants.map₁.toList do
    12	    let n' := (privateToUserName? n).getD n
    13	    if (`Agent).isPrefixOf n' && (!n.isInternal || isPrivateName n) then
    14	      let s := n.toString
    15	      if (s.splitOn "match_").length > 1 || (s.splitOn "proof_").length > 1 then continue
    16	      match ci with
    17	      | .defnInfo _ => defs := defs.push n
    18	      | .opaqueInfo _ => defs := defs.push n
    19	      | .thmInfo _ => thms := thms.push n
    20	      | _ => pure ()
    21	  return (defs.qsort (fun a b => a.toString < b.toString), thms.qsort (fun a b => a.toString < b.toString))
    22	
    23	def stdOnly (axc : IO.Ref (Std.HashMap Name Bool)) (n : Name) : CoreM Bool := do
    24	  match (← axc.get).get? n with
    25	  | some b => return b
    26	  | none =>
    27	    let ax ← collectAxioms n
    28	    let b := ax.all (fun a => a == ``propext || a == ``Classical.choice || a == ``Quot.sound)
    29	    axc.modify (·.insert n b)
    30	    return b
    31	
    32	partial def tryClose (axc : IO.Ref (Std.HashMap Name Bool)) (thms : Array Name) (g : MVarId) (fuel : Nat) : MetaM Bool := do
    33	  if fuel == 0 then return false
    34	  g.withContext do
    35	    let s0 ← saveState
    36	    -- assumption
    37	    try
    38	      g.assumption
    39	      return true
    40	    catch _ => s0.restore
    41	    -- apply an agent theorem, close premises
    42	    for t in thms do
    43	      if !(← stdOnly axc t) then continue
    44	      let s ← saveState
    45	      try
    46	        let c ← mkConstWithFreshMVarLevels t
    47	        let gs ← g.apply c
    48	        let mut ok := true
    49	        for g' in gs do
    50	          if !(← g'.isAssigned) then
    51	            if !(← tryClose axc thms g' (fuel - 1)) then
    52	              ok := false
    53	              break
    54	        if ok then return true

     2	# usage: python3 gold_name_check.py <log_dir> <exp145_dir> [<exp142_bridges_dir>]
     3	import csv, json, re, sys, os, collections
     4	logd, exp = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
     5	br = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else None
     6	LT = '\r\n' if b'\r\n' in open(f'{exp}/results/per_run.csv','rb').read(2000) else '\n'
     7	rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(f'{exp}/results/per_run.csv', newline='')))
     8	orig_cols = list(rows[0].keys())
     9	out = {}
    10	for r in rows:
    11	    if r['lean_entails_raw'] != '1':
    12	        continue
    13	    m = r['mod']; p = f'{logd}/{m}.log'
    14	    res = dict(run=r['run'], solver=r['solver'], task=r['task'], mod=m)
    15	    if not os.path.exists(p):
    16	        res.update(status='no_log', all_gold_names_proved=0, reason='no log'); out[m] = res; continue
    17	    t = open(p).read()
    18	    exit0 = bool(re.search(r'(?m)^exit 0$', t))
    19	    err = bool(re.search(r'(?m)^\S+:\d+:\d+: error', t))
    20	    g = re.findall(r'GCHK (\S+) (\w+)(.*)', t)
    21	    s = re.search(r'GSUMMARY gold=(\d+) proved=(\d+) dup_last_components=(\d+)', t)

    23	    for nm, k, d in g:
    24	        st[k].append(nm if (not d.strip() or k=='OK') else f'{nm} {d.strip()}')
    25	    res.update(compiled_ok=exit0 and not err, gold_total=int(s.group(1)) if s else None,
    26	               proved=int(s.group(2)) if s else None, dup_last_components=int(s.group(3)) if s else None,
    27	               missing=st['MISSING'], nonstd_axioms=st['NONSTD'], not_theorem=st['NOT_THEOREM'],
    28	               private_helpers=st['PRIVATE_HELPER'], structure_fields=st['STRUCTURE_FIELD'], nested_aux=st['NESTED_AUX'], gold_names=[x for k in ('OK','MISSING','NONSTD','NOT_THEOREM') for x in st[k]])
    29	    ok = (res['compiled_ok'] and s is not None and res['gold_total'] > 0 and res['gold_total'] == res['proved']
    30	          and not st['MISSING'] and not st['NONSTD'] and not st['NOT_THEOREM'] and True)
    31	    res['all_gold_names_proved'] = int(ok)
    32	    reasons = []
    33	    if not res['compiled_ok']: reasons.append('bridge did not compile cleanly in the check')
    34	    if s is None: reasons.append('no GSUMMARY')
    35	    elif res['gold_total'] == 0: reasons.append('no gold theorem found')
    36	    if st['MISSING']: reasons.append('missing/renamed/unproved: ' + ', '.join(st['MISSING']))
    37	    if st['NONSTD']: reasons.append('non-standard axioms: ' + ', '.join(st['NONSTD']))
    38	    if st['NOT_THEOREM']: reasons.append('not a theorem: ' + ', '.join(st['NOT_THEOREM']))
    39	    res['reason'] = '; '.join(reasons)

    45	        except Exception:

    47	    out[m] = res

    54	    else:

    58	# per-solver before/after
    59	tab = collections.OrderedDict()
    60	for r in rows:
    61	    d = tab.setdefault(r['solver'], dict(runs=0, accepted=0, counted_1to4=0, counted_all5=0, cond5_fail_among_accepted=0, cond5_fail_among_counted=0))
    62	    d['runs'] += 1

     2	import Lean

     5	elab "#gold_check" : command => do
     6	  let env ← getEnv
     7	  -- 1. collect named gold theorems (public, user-written, not structure fields, not nested auxiliaries)
     8	  let mut cands : Array (Name × Name) := #[]

    11	    if (`Gold).isPrefixOf n' && (!nm.isInternal || isPrivateName nm) then
    12	      match ci with
    13	      | .thmInfo _ =>
    14	        let aux := match nm.eraseMacroScopes with
    15	          | .str _ l => l.startsWith "match_" || l.startsWith "proof_"
    16	          | _ => false
    17	        if aux then continue
    18	        let rng ← findDeclarationRanges? nm
    19	        if rng.isNone then continue
    20	        if isPrivateName nm then
    21	          logInfo m!"GCHK {n'} PRIVATE_HELPER"
    22	          continue
    23	        let pre := n'.getPrefix
    24	        -- structure field proofs (e.g. `Foo.nonempty` of a structure field) are not named theorems
    25	        match getStructureInfo? env pre with
    26	        | some si =>
    27	          if si.fieldNames.contains (match n' with | .str _ s => Name.mkSimple s | _ => Name.anonymous) then
    28	            logInfo m!"GCHK {n'} STRUCTURE_FIELD"
    29	            continue
    30	        | none => pure ()
    31	        -- nested auxiliary (let rec / local lemma lifted out of another declaration)
    32	        match env.find? pre with
    33	        | some (.thmInfo _) | some (.defnInfo _) =>
    34	          logInfo m!"GCHK {n'} NESTED_AUX"
    35	          continue
    36	        | _ => pure ()
    37	        cands := cands.push (nm, n')
    38	      | _ => pure ()
    39	    else pure ()
    40	  let lastOf := fun (n : Name) => match n with | .str _ s => s | _ => n.toString
    41	  let lasts := cands.map (fun p => lastOf p.2)

    45	    let dupl := (lasts.filter (· == l)).size > 1
    46	    let parentLast := match n'.getPrefix with | .str _ s => s | _ => ""
    47	    let plain := Name.mkStr `Bridge ("G_" ++ l)
    48	    let qual := Name.mkStr `Bridge ("G_" ++ parentLast ++ "_" ++ l)

import re
words=set(w.strip().lower() for w in open('/usr/share/dict/words'))
extra=set("brier bernoulli lean mathlib veribench vals valkyrie tiny256 json csv sha256 logistic bootstrap resamples resample resampled kendall spearman pearson auroc prover provers theorem theorems entailment entails countermodel countermodels adapter adapters satisfiable unsatisfiable axiom axioms propext preregistration prespecified nonnegative uv numpy scipy runbook readme github google tldr ttj astra opus codex fable terminus gpt sol goedel deepseek vllm koyejo gneiting raftery jasa mae roc tc fsc ci utc iso nonce forall allowlisted admissions workstream subagent reanalysis elaborated kernel checker checkers bridge bridges obligation obligations typecheck vacuously vacuous repair repairs timeout timeouts reproducible unverified unmodified allowlist md py lean4 ok ids id dispatcher inference inputs outputs prepro ordinal binary logits ridge coefficients misc www http https docs doc edit tab gpu subscription tokens token metadata snapshot snapshots blobs blob hashes hash checkpoint pilot pilots forecasting forecaster forecast forecasts feasibility retrospective screening prevalence covariate receipts receipt manifest decidable immutable invariants invariant transport transported dataset datasets ungrounded preexisting rerun reruns refit refits workflow workflows rubric certificates certificate satisfiability faithfulness falsifiable overclaim lemmas lemma namespace namespaced autoimplicit heartbeat".split())
def check(path):
    t=open(path).read()
    t=re.sub(r'```.*?```','',t,flags=re.S)
    t=re.sub(r'`[^`]*`','',t)
    t=re.sub(r'https?://\S+','',t)
    t=re.sub(r'<!--.*?-->','',t,flags=re.S)
    toks=re.findall(r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z'-]+",t)
    bad=set()
    for w in toks:
        lw=w.lower().strip("'-")
        if lw in words or lw in extra: continue
        if re.search(r'[A-Z]',w[1:]) : continue  # CamelCase identifiers
        if lw.endswith('s') and lw[:-1] in words|extra: continue
        if lw.endswith('ed') and (lw[:-2] in words|extra or lw[:-1] in words|extra): continue
        if lw.endswith('ing') and (lw[:-3] in words|extra or lw[:-3]+'e' in words|extra): continue
        if lw.endswith('ly') and lw[:-2] in words|extra: continue
        bad.add(w)
    print(path, sorted(bad))
for f in ['README.md','PROTOCOL.md','SOURCE_AUDIT.md','RESULTS.md','RUNBOOK.md','CKPT_prover_target.md','prompts/binary_forecast.md']:
    check(f)
EOF

input.command:
uv run --python 3.12 --with numpy==2.4.2 --with scipy==1.17.0 python - <<'EOF'
import json,csv,collections,numpy as np,sys
sys.path.insert(0,'experiments/03_prover_target_fsc_judge/scripts')
from analyze import corr, metrics, fit_map
from scipy.special import expit
S='private/prover_target/source/experiments/'
labels=list(csv.DictReader(open(S+'145_entailment_vacuity_axiom_check_tiny256_11-01-2026/results/per_run.csv')))
scores={r['cell']:float(r['tc']) for r in json.load(open(S+'140_entailment_check_vs_theorem_coverage_tiny256_10-31-2026/manifest_tiny256.json'))}
split=json.load(open('private/prover_target/split_manifest.json'))
split_of={t:s for s,ts in split.items() for t in ts}
rows=[dict(task=r['task'],solver=r['solver'],tc=scores[r['run']],y=int(r['counted_all5']),s=split_of[r['task']]) for r in labels]
res=json.load(open('experiments/03_prover_target_fsc_judge/results/retrospective.json'))
b0,b1=res['conditions']['all_agents']['candidates'][0]['coefficients']
print("1) corr() on exactly-constant vectors:")
y=np.array([r['y'] for r in rows if r['s']=='test'],float)
for prev in (205/256, 157/192, 149/192):
    q=np.full(len(y),prev); print(f"   prevalence={prev:.10f} -> pearson={corr(q,y)!r}")
print("2) mapped probability per tc level (pooled fit):")
for tc in sorted({r['tc'] for r in rows}): print(f"   tc={tc:.1f} -> q={expit(b0+b1*tc):.3f}")
print("3) tc level distribution and empirical acceptance by split:")
for s in ('train','validation','test'):
    c=collections.Counter(r['tc'] for r in rows if r['s']==s); n=sum(c.values())
    print(f"   {s}: n={n}, share tc=1.0: {c[1.0]/n:.3f}, levels present: {sorted(c)}")
    for tc in sorted(c):
        ys=[r['y'] for r in rows if r['s']==s and r['tc']==tc]
        print(f"      tc={tc:.1f}: n={len(ys):3d} accept={np.mean(ys):.3f}")
print("4) stronger untrained baseline: per-solver training prevalence on test (pooled):")
test=[r for r in rows if r['s']=='test']
train=[r for r in rows if r['s']=='train']
prev_s={s:np.mean([r['y'] for r in train if r['solver']==s]) for s in sorted({r['solver'] for r in rows})}
print("   per-solver train prevalence:", {k:round(v,4) for k,v in prev_s.items()})
yt=np.array([r['y'] for r in test],float)
q_solver=np.array([prev_s[r['solver']] for r in test]); q_map=expit(b0+b1*np.array([r['tc'] for r in test])); q_const=np.full(len(test),np.mean([r['y'] for r in train]))
for name,q in (('mapped',q_map),('constant',q_const),('per_solver_constant',q_solver)):
    print(f"   {name}: brier={np.mean((q-yt)**2):.4f}")
print("5) two-feature map (tc + solver one-hot) fitted on train, evaluated on test (informational):")
sol=sorted(prev_s)
def design(rs): return np.column_stack([np.array([r['tc'] for r in rs])]+[np.array([1.0 if r['solver']==s else 0.0 for r in rs]) for s in sol[1:]])
from scipy.optimize import minimize
X=design(train); Y=np.array([r['y'] for r in train],float)
def obj(beta):
    D=np.column_stack((np.ones(len(X)),X)); l=D@beta; return np.mean(np.logaddexp(0,l)-Y*l), D.T@(expit(l)-Y)/len(Y)
f=minimize(obj,np.zeros(X.shape[1]+1),jac=True,method='BFGS'); Dt=np.column_stack((np.ones(len(test)),design(test)))
print(f"   brier={np.mean((expit(Dt@f.x)-yt)**2):.4f} (converged={f.success})")
print("6) within-task vs between-task: test tasks where all 4 solvers agree on outcome:")
bytask=collections.defaultdict(list)
for r in test: bytask[r['task']].append(r['y'])
agree=sum(1 for v in bytask.values() if len(set(v))==1); print(f"   {agree}/128 test tasks have identical outcome across the 4 solvers")
EOF

The light QA (quality assurance) round for `experiments/03_prover_target_fsc_judge/` at commit 6b288c7 passes: zero critical and two major findings, nine minor ones. The verdict is at `private/prover_target/review/verdict.md`, and no reviewed file was touched.

**What held up.** The result reproduces exactly and every source-audit number checks against the raw evidence.
- **Sources:** all 17 pinned blobs hash-match both the private snapshot and git at the pinned revision of the private `brando90/veribench` repository.
- **Counts:** the per-run CSV gives 1,024 artifacts, 840 raw acceptances, 801 after conditions 1 to 4, 789 after condition 5. The 39 and 12 drops are exactly the native_decide and missing-gold-name rows.
- **Reproduction:** the full analysis re-run with uv, numpy 2.4.2 and scipy 1.17.0 in an isolated copy is byte-identical to the committed results JSON, provenance file and rendered RESULTS.md. The verifier passes. The protocol and config are unchanged since the pre-analysis commit 24c9152.
- **Statistics:** the Brier identity is correct, and the task-clustered paired bootstrap, area under the curve, rank correlations and validation-only selection match the protocol. Brier loss here means the mean squared error of a probability forecast against a 0/1 outcome.
- **Claims:** no fresh-validation or semantic-oracle claim appears anywhere. The "no human count needed" claim is valid, because the feature is the judge-produced formal specification coverage (FSC) score, as the source 140 README states.
- **Lean checkers:** AxLib and WitLib make the label depend on candidate proofs, and GoldChkLib never compares the bridge statement type. The audit describes them correctly.

**Major findings for the builder.**
1. **World-editable Google Doc link in a public repo.** The commit adds a link to the human-study plan in two public files. Drive reports its sharing as anyone with the link can edit. Remove the URL from the public files, or restrict sharing first. The private snapshot holds no email addresses, so this is an integrity exposure, not an identity leak.
2. **Wrong integrity statistic quoted for the exact label.** The audit cites 8 of 72 forged-audit acceptances for a different checker. The source's own evidence for the label's gate class is 155 of 212 constructed invalid bridges accepted by the names-and-axioms gate, and the 145 README says conditions 1 to 5 do not block gold-proof reuse. Add those facts.

**Minor findings.** A floating-point quirk reports Pearson 0.0 instead of null for the constant forecast in two conditions. The ridge grid is so coarse that validation selection did no work. Calibration is uneven by score level, with 0.75 predicted versus 0.39 observed at score 0.9. Mean absolute error is an improper score and should not carry a ranking arrow. By a name heuristic, 26 of 128 test tasks have a safe or unsafe sibling in train or validation. The exposure disclosure, the word "ratings" for a judge score, the unnamed pause-file paths and one wording slip round out the list.

Ranked next steps:
- [p 9/10] Builder removes or re-permissions the Google Doc link before any push, because the repository is public.
- [p 8/10] Builder adds the 155 of 212 and gold-proof-reuse facts to the source audit and results limits, because they change how a reader weighs the label.
- [p 5/10] Builder applies the nine minor items and reruns the RUNBOOK checks, no second review per the light-QA rule.
- [p 3/10] Brando decides whether the human-study plan doc should stay editor-shared at all.

**TLDR-end:** [ttj: experiments/03_prover_target_fsc_judge/ prover-target forecasting study › light QA review] The zero-call retrospective result reproduces byte-for-byte and passes review with 0 critical and 2 major findings.
